meta.title: MRA arm and claw from the CAD alone
meta.naming: Part names are CAD mesh names (ARA_xx), NOT the codes engraved on the wood. Ids are the top-level instances NAUOn.
meta.units: mm, assembly space, Y up. The arm lies in XY planes (plates normal to Z); -Z side = CAD R6 NAUO15 side, +Z side = CAD R5 NAUO14 side.

direction_notes.+arm: along the upper arm, shoulder to elbow, in the CAD pose
direction_notes.+armN: normal of the cross plate A11 (forward and down)
direction_notes.+n: claw plate normal (up through C9, C4, C3)
direction_notes.+fore: along the forearm, elbow to wrist, in the CAD pose

meta.method: trimesh on the full-detail GLB; plate outlines from mid-plane sections; screws by radial ray casts along their axes; contacts by dense surface samples (closest-point distance < 0.25 mm); slide-out and order tests with tools/stepgen.py blocked(); threaded screws are not tested with blocked() because the thread overlaps the wood by design.

NAUO45.name: MG90S
NAUO45.drives: the turret: the horn is held still in the base plates, so the servo and the whole turret turn on it
NAUO45.held_by: R1 NAUO10 (the ears rest on its top face, y = 102.96; the case hangs through a 12.5 x 22.7 mm cut-out, x 157.4-169.9, z 124.1-146.8, with a 5.7 x 6.4 mm extension at the lead end and a 1.0 mm slit to the edge of R1) and R2 NAUO11 (a 12.5 mm wide notch open at its bottom edge, x 157.4-169.9, y 103.0-123.3, that straddles the case; 0.00 mm gap)
NAUO45.inserted: shaft pointing down, through R1 from above; R2 then comes down over the case
NAUO45.horn: NAUO46 (double-ended, 36.3 mm tip to tip, arms along +Z and -Z)
NAUO45.horn_fixed_to: lies in a horn-shaped pocket cut through B2 NAUO2 (y 90.53-93.53) and dips 0.67 mm into a matching 37.5 x 8.0 mm hole in B1 NAUO1; no screw touches it; B2 is clamped to B1 by the six M3x6 screws NAUO47-52

NAUO58.name: MG90S
NAUO58.job: elbow (forearm) servo, on the -Z side of the turret
NAUO58.drives: the three-layer lever A1 + A2 + A2_Supplement (NAUO18, 19, 20), which moves the forearm through link A3 NAUO21 and the rear end of A4 NAUO22

NAUO72.drives: the jaw CAD ARA_C8 NAUO39; the other jaw CAD ARA_C7 NAUO38 is geared to it

forced: Screw NAUO55 goes in before the lever and before servo NAUO58: its driver path runs through the servo cut-out of R6 and is blocked by horn NAUO59 and servo NAUO58.
The lever goes on before servo NAUO58: the shaft tip (z 120.35) and the head of NAUO55 (z 123.50) are 3.15 mm apart and the 9 mm lever must engage 2.8 mm on one and 3.0 mm on the other.
Screw NAUO56 goes into the lever before the lever is in the turret (R6 is 2.5 mm from its head), or with the lever swung up above the top edge of R6.
Servo before clamp plate before clamp screws, on both sides.
Claw: servo NAUO72 into C3 before C5 and C6; C5 and C6 before (or with) C4; screws NAUO74/75 before C9; jaws before C9; C9 before screw NAUO76.
alternatives: Servo NAUO66 with R7 can be fitted before the upper arm: the arm then comes down 3 mm to the -Z side of its seat and is pushed +Z onto the shaft (tested free).
A3 and screw NAUO62 can be added after the lever is in, with the lever swung up so the hole is above the top edge of R6 (y 175.4).
The triangle A8 can be mounted alone and A7, A9, A10 added to it on the model (each tested free), instead of building the linkage in the hand.
C9 can go on after the clips C1 / C2 (pushed up onto the prong tips) instead of before them.
A4 can be screwed to C2, and A9 / A10 to C1, with the claw off the arm (tested free), instead of sliding the finished claw into the fork.

NAUO16.note: Clamp plate, 35.7 x 25.1 mm. Servo cut-out 23.2 x 12.3 mm with a 1 x 8 mm notch in one short end, two 2.8 mm holes. Identical to NAUO17. Looks the same flipped top to bottom, not end for end (the notch). Engraved face outwards (+Z). Its notch is at the lead end of servo NAUO66.

NAUO17.note: Clamp plate, identical to NAUO16. Engraved face outwards (-Z). In the CAD its notch is at the -X end, the opposite end from the lead of servo NAUO58 (which leaves at +X): it is modelled turned end for end compared with NAUO16. Guess: on the real kit the notch goes over the lead.

NAUO18.note: Inner layer of the lever (next to A5). Holes, from the shoulder end: 5.74 mm (fits over the 5.5 mm head of screw NAUO55), 2.3 mm (thread for NAUO56), 2.8 mm (free on NAUO62). Engraved face (-Z) is covered by A2. Must be the innermost of the three layers.

NAUO19.note: Middle layer of the lever. Horn-shaped pocket at the shoulder end, then two 2.8 mm holes. Engraved face (-Z) is covered by A2_Supplement.

NAUO20.note: Outer layer of the lever (faces R6). Horn-shaped pocket, 2.8 mm hole, and a 5.58 mm hole at the end that the head of screw NAUO62 sinks into. Engraved face outwards (-Z). Must be the outermost layer. Not a loose spacer: it is clamped into the lever by NAUO56 and carries part of the horn.

NAUO21.note: Plain link 90 x 10 mm, two 2.3 mm (threaded) holes 80.0 mm apart. Looks the same any way round or up. Lies in the same layer as A5, between A1 (lever end) / A4 (top end) on the outside and nothing on the inside.

NAUO22.note: Forearm strip on the -Z side, 125 x 10 mm, three 2.8 mm holes in a line: 35.0 mm then 80.0 mm. The short end goes to A3, the long end to the claw. Looks the same flipped about its length; not end for end. Lies on the outer faces of A3, A5 and C2.

NAUO23.note: Upper arm, -Z side, 92 x 12 mm. From the shoulder: 2.8 mm pivot hole, slot, 2.8 mm hole for the M3x16 (37.9 mm from the pivot), slot, 2.3 mm (threaded) elbow hole at 80.0 mm. Looks the same flipped about its length (only the engraving changes side); not end for end. Same outline as A6 but not interchangeable with it.

NAUO24.note: Upper arm, +Z side, 92 x 12 mm. Horn-shaped pocket at the shoulder end, slot, 2.8 mm hole for the M3x16 (49.8 mm from the pivot, i.e. 12 mm further along than on A5), slot, 2.3 mm elbow hole. Engraved face outwards (+Z).

NAUO25.note: Rear link 90 x 10 mm, holes 80.0 mm apart: 2.3 mm (threaded) at the turret end, 2.8 mm at the A8 end. The same strip as A3 except for that one hole size, so it has a right way round. Engraved face (+Z) towards R5.

NAUO26.note: Triangle plate 56 x 27.5 mm. Holes: 2.8 mm (elbow), 2.3 mm (A7 corner), 2.3 mm (A9 corner), and a 4.0 mm triangle cut-out 5.4 mm from the A9 hole. No symmetry: one way only. A7, A9 and A10 all lie on its engraved (+Z) face.

NAUO27.note: Levelling link 90 x 10 mm, two 2.8 mm holes 80.0 mm apart, and a 3.3 mm triangle cut-out 7.7 mm from one hole. The triangle end goes to the triangle-marked corner of A8. Engraved face outwards (+Z).

NAUO28.note: Forearm strip on the +Z side, 90 x 10 mm, two 2.8 mm holes 80.0 mm apart, and a 2.6 mm square cut-out 8.9 mm from one hole. The square end is at the elbow. Same strip as A9 apart from the mark. Engraved face outwards (+Z).

NAUO29.note: Cross plate of the upper arm, 66.8 x 36.2 mm, two 10 mm tabs on each long edge (29.9 mm between the shoulders = the gap between A5 and A6). Two cross-shaped slots, one open to the A5 edge and one to the A6 edge, 12 mm apart along the arm, take the two T-pieces and the M3x16 screws. Two 8 x 8 mm holes: the claw servo lead is modelled passing through both. Looks the same turned half a turn in its own plane, but NOT flipped over: the engraved face must look up and back, direction [-0.74, 0.67, 0] in the CAD pose, or the slots are 12 mm away from the screw holes in A5 and A6.

NAUO30.note: T-piece ("A12" in the CAD), 25 x 11.7 mm: bar 25 x 6.4 mm, stem 7.2 x 5.3 mm with a 2.3 mm hole. It is the wooden nut for screw NAUO53: the stem goes through the lower cross-slot of A11 from A11's engraved face and the screw threads through the hole. Not a spacer. Left-right symmetric, so either face can be up (engraved face +Z in the CAD).

NAUO31.note: Second T-piece, identical to NAUO30, in the upper cross-slot of A11, nut for screw NAUO54. Same orientation as NAUO30 in the CAD.

NAUO32.note: Clip plate on the +Z side of the claw. Body sits on top of C3; two sprung prongs (10.3 mm over both, 1.0 mm slit between) go down through C3, C4 and C9; shoulders rest on C9 and one 1.1 mm barb hooks under it; a tooth at the front drops into an edge notch of C3; a leg at the back hangs behind C3 and carries the wrist hole. Two 2.3 mm (threaded) holes: A10 (in the leg) and A9 (in the body). Engraved face outwards (+Z).

NAUO33.note: Clip plate on the -Z side. Same outline as C1, the same way round (not a mirror image as it sits), but only one 2.3 mm hole (A4, in the leg). Engraved on the opposite face (-Z, outwards), so with engraved faces up on the table C1 and C2 are mirror images.

NAUO34.note: Servo plate of the claw, 58.2 x 47.7 mm. Servo cut-out 23.2 x 12.3 mm with the lead notch at its -Z end; 10 x 6.3 mm cable hole in the tongue at the back; slots for C1, C2 + C5 (a 6 mm wide double slot), C6; two 2.3 mm (threaded) holes for the M3x16 screws; two open notches in the front edge for the teeth of C1 and C2. Engraved on its underside (the face the servo ears touch). One way only.

NAUO35.note: Keyhole plate, 47.7 x 46.5 mm, under the servo. Keyhole notch open to the front edge for the shaft and horn hub; two 2.8 mm holes for the M3x16 screws; 2.3 mm (threaded) hole for the jaw pivot; slots as C3. Engraved on its underside (towards the jaws). One way only.

NAUO36.note: Spacer bar between C3 and C4 on the -Z side, 40.4 x 16.9 mm. Tabs 7.6 mm wide (it shares the 6 mm double slots with the prongs of C2). A shoulder on its top edge sits under the servo ear. Engraved face outwards (-Z). Not interchangeable with NAUO37.

NAUO37.note: Spacer bar between C3 and C4 on the +Z side. Tabs 10 mm wide; an extra notch in its lower edge clears the tip of the jaw pivot screw NAUO76. Engraved face outwards (+Z).

NAUO38.note: Jaw with a 2.8 mm pivot hole and gear teeth; turns on screw NAUO76 between C4 and C9. Engraved on its underside.

NAUO39.note: Jaw with the horn-shaped pocket and gear teeth; driven by the servo horn. Engraved on its underside.

NAUO40.note: Bottom cover, 47.6 x 40.4 mm. 11.67 mm hole on the servo shaft axis, 2.8 mm hole for the jaw pivot screw, two 7.8 x 3 mm slots for the clips. The outline is symmetric but the holes are not: one way only. Engraved on its underside (outer face). It hides the heads of screws NAUO74 and NAUO75.

cad_oddities: Clamp plate CAD R8 (NAUO17) has its 1 x 8 mm lead notch at the -X end; the lead of its servo NAUO58 leaves at the +X end. On the other side R7 (NAUO16) has notch and lead at the same end. NAUO17 is the same plate modelled turned end for end.

The shoulder pivot screw NAUO55 is at [175.33, 161.90] and the two shoulder servo shafts at [175.66, 162.28]: 0.50 mm apart in the CAD, although they are one axis in the mechanism. The cut-outs of R5 / R6 give the servo case only 0.2 mm of play lengthways and 0.15 mm across, so the play does not take it up.
No screw is modelled for any servo horn (the small screw into the end of the shaft), and no nuts: every M3 screw threads into a 2.3 mm hole in the wood.

Horn NAUO59 overlaps its pocket in A2 / A2_Supplement by up to 0.20 mm and horn NAUO73 overlaps the pocket in the jaw by up to 0.35 mm; horn NAUO67 has 0.15 mm clearance in A6. The CAD horn is a straight 6.6 mm bar; the pockets are tapered.
The heads of screws NAUO74 / NAUO75 are 3.02 mm high in the 3.00 mm jaw layer, so C9 is drawn resting on them (0.02 mm overlap).
The servo label is modelled 0.30 mm thick and stands 0.10 mm outside the cut-out of R7 / R8; collision tests here use the servo case and shaft only.

Each servo has three rigid 3 mm lead stubs (0.5 mm on the claw servo); the flexible leads are the separate "ARA_Pathways" parts (NAUO87 base, NAUO88 servo NAUO58, NAUO89 servo NAUO66, NAUO94 claw). Collision tests here ignore the stubs.
The tip of screw NAUO56 stands 1.0 mm proud of the inner face of A1, into the layer of A5 and A3; it is clear of both in the CAD pose.

With the turret complete the lever has only 2.55 mm of sideways room in the CAD pose (head of NAUO56 to R6) but needs 3.0 mm to come on or off the head of NAUO55; it has the room when swung 40 to 90 degrees up.
open_questions: Does TechBox fit the shoulder servos and the lever before or after the turret side plates (CAD R5 / R6) are on? The existing guide finishes the turret first; the CAD then forces the order upper arm, screw NAUO55, lever, servo NAUO58, R8 on the -Z side. If a side plate goes on later, the lever and its servo could ride in on it.
Are the servo horns screwed to the shafts in the real kit? Nothing in the CAD says so, and on the -Z side the head of NAUO55 sits where the driver would have to go.
Which way round does the real R8 clamp plate go (notch over the lead)?
Does TechBox fit the clip plates C1 / C2 to the claw before it goes on the arm (as proposed here), and is C9 snapped on before or after them? Both orders pass the collision test.
The engraved text read from the CAD pockets differs from the CAD part names for 17 of the 25 arm and claw plates; the codes report is the authority on which name the guide shows.
